gr.description: Βαρομετρικό χαμηλό από τη Μεσόγειο φέρνει νέο κύμα κακοκαιρίας την Κυριακή. Σε υψηλά για την εποχή επίπεδα η θερμοκρασία. Άστατος θα διατηρηθεί ο καιρός σήμερα Παρασκευή, με τοπικές βροχές και σποραδικές καταιγίδες να εκδηλώνονται κυρίως στη Μακεδονία, τη Θράκη, το βορειοανατολικό Αιγαίο, τις Σποράδες, την Εύβοια και την Αττική. Πρόσκαιρες, ασθενείς βροχοπτώσεις αναμένονται επίσης στα ορεινά της Κρήτης και τις Κυκλάδες. Στην υπόλοιπη χώρα θα υπάρχουν νεφώσεις με διαστήματα ηλιοφάνειας, ενώ η αφρικανική σκόνη θα παραμείνει σε χαμηλά επίπεδα. Η θερμοκρασία θα διατηρηθεί σε υψηλά για την εποχή επίπεδα, φτάνοντας έως τους 26°C (16-25°C στην Αττική και 13-22°C στη Θεσσαλονίκη). Σύμφωνα με τον Γιάννη Καλλιάνο, παρόμοιο θα είναι το σκηνικό και το Σάββατο, με περιορισμένα φαινόμενα στα νότια του Αιγαίου, τη δυτική ηπειρωτική χώρα και την Πελοπόννησο. Από την Κυριακή, όμως, αναμένεται υποτροπή του καιρού, καθώς βαρομετρικό χαμηλό από τη Μεσόγειο φέρνει νέο κύμα κακοκαιρίας. Τα ισχυρά φαινόμενα θα ξεκινήσουν από το Ιόνιο και σταδιακά θα επεκταθούν στην υπόλοιπη χώρα, επηρεάζοντας έντονα τα δυτικά, τα βορειοδυτικά, αλλά και την Αττική. Η κακοκαιρία θα γενικευτεί τη Δευτέρα και θα διαρκέσει 2 έως 3 ημέρες. Οι νότιοι άνεμοι στα πελάγη θα πνέουν έντασης 4-5 μποφόρ, ενώ ο υδράργυρος θα σημειώσει μικρή πτώση, κυμαινόμενος μεταξύ 20 και 24°C. #ΚΑΙΡΟΣ #ΚΑΚΟΚΑΙΡΙΑ

co.title: ¿Cómo avanza el plan de choque de salud de De la Espriella? Ya se ha resuelto el 51 % de casos por medicamentos
co.description: La ministra de Salud, Ana María Vesga, dio detalles sobre el plan de choque anunciado hace un mes tras un Consejo de Ministros y resaltó los avances en la entrega de medicamentos y la atención de procedimientos. El informe lo compartió en el Congreso de Cajas de Compensación Familiar que se celebra en Cartagena. Desde este evento, recordó que con esta primera fase del plan se busca garantizar la continuidad de tratamientos y resolver aquellos pendientes que están acumulados. Respecto a los casos pendientes por medicamentos, la ministra informó que se logró el cierre de estos para el 51 % de los pacientes, pues se registran 307.369 personas con entregas completadas de un grupo de 602.117 que estaba a la espera. En cuanto a las unidades entregadas, este va en un 42,89 % que en términos de cifras equivale a 12.514.638, estando pendientes 29.179.262. La población que está pendiente se concentra mayoritariamente, según Vesga, en un 50 % en Bogotá, Antioquia, Valle del Cauca, Cundinamarca y Norte de Santander. Para aquellos pacientes que sus enfermedades requieren medicamentos más costoso, la ministra Vesga explicó en una rueda de prensa tras su intervención que en el plan de choque lo que se hizo fue identificar junto a sociedades científicas cerca de 20 patologías que tienen mayor riesgo de vida o una ventana terapéutica más corta, además de quienes se pueden desestabilizar fácilmente. Lea también: Así será el “plan de choque” para el sistema de salud que arrancaría este mes En ese grupo se identificaron como enfermedades de alta hospitalización el EPOC, el asma, la insuficiencia cardíaca, la enfermedad renal crónica, lo relacionado con la salud mental y las gestantes con tratamientos esenciales como diabetes gestacional o hipertensión. Con un riesgo vital o de pérdida de tratamiento, el plan identificó a los pacientes trasplantados o que padecen cáncer, VIH, diabetes insulinodependiente, enfermedades neurodegenerativas y enfermedades huérfanas como la hemofilia y la hipertensión arterial pulmonar. Con esas características, se identificaron 1.600.000 pacientes que están siendo atendidos con urgencia. “Más de 5 mil pacientes de enfermedades huérfanas desatendidos en el último periodo, eso nos habla de sufrimiento en los pacientes, de sufrimiento en las familias y esa es nuestra primera promesa, volver a poner a los pacientes en el centro de las decisiones del sistema”, aludió la ministra sobre los problemas de la pasada administración. Vesga relató ante los medios que el plan de choque tiene una duración de tres meses. Sobre los recursos, afirmó que ya están asegurados en Adres, por lo que se pagan de manera directa a través de giros directos. Para que no hayan temas de corrupción en cuanto a los giros, la ministra reiteró la intención desde el Gobierno Nacional para que cada recurso esté atado a una factura y que esta sea auditada y esté ligada a un servicio prestado. “Lo que hemos encontrado es que el sistema (2:32) carga con un montón de desorden entre las relaciones entre aseguradores, prestadores, proveedores; las facturas que se presentan, no se auditan, se pagan anticipos, hay glosas; todo ese desorden necesitamos ponerlo en orden, es decir, factura que se presta, factura que se audita, factura que se revisa si es el caso y factura que se paga”, reiteró Vesga. Para cumplir y resolver los casos pendientes de los procedimientos, el Ministerio de Salud seguirá haciendo vigilancia al 87 % de los registros pendientes, además de que las verificaciones periódicas de entrega e historia clínica se extenderán hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2026 para asegurar que no se cierren casos en papel sin una atención médica efectiva. El plan de choque de tres meses es solo una parte del plan para enfrentar la crisis en la salud, pues otra de las acciones que se evaluará es el cálculo de una Unidad de Pago por Capitación (UPC) justa que evite que las EPS tengan que ir a liquidación. La ministra dejó claro que las intervenciones a las EPS deberían ser el último paso. “Necesitamos ser creativos y necesitamos emplear toda la capacidad jurídica, regulatoria para poder evitar esas liquidaciones que históricamente lo que hacen es erosionar más la confianza en el sistema y sobre todo causan enormes daños a la atención de la población”, subrayó Vesga. bd.title: Harbour BioMed Receives China NMPA Approval of Batoclimab Injection (Subcutaneous Injection) for the Treatment of Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
bd.description: The first NMPA-approved anti-FcRn therapy to complete its full clinical development for gMG patients in China CAMBRIDGE, Mass., ROTTERDAM, Netherlands and SHANGHAI, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbour BioMed (the "Company"; HKEX: 02142), a global biopharmaceutical company committed to the discovery and development of novel antibody therapeutics in immunology, oncology and other areas, today announced that the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China has approved the Biologics License Application (BLA) for batoclimab injection (subcutaneous injection) (batoclimab SC), 170 mg (1 mL)/vial, for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive. The approval is supported by positive results from a pivotal Phase 3 clinical study conducted at 27 centers in China. The main study population was patients with generalized myasthenia gravis who were positive for acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Ab) or muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies (MuSK-Ab). The primary endpoint of the study was the proportion of the population with sustained improvement in the Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living Scale (MG-ADL) score during the first cycle of treatment. Sustained improvement was defined as a reduction in MG-ADL score of ≥ 3 points from baseline that persisted for at least 4 weeks. 58.2% of patients treated with batoclimab SC achieved the primary endpoint, which was significantly higher compared with 31.3% in the placebo group (P=0.001). Treatment effect was observed as early as the second week of therapy. Additionally, batoclimab SC group demonstrated significant improvements in secondary endpoints compared with placebo group, including sustained Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) improvement (64.2% vs 40.6%; P=0.008), duration of 3-point or greater MG-ADL improvement (51.5% vs 36.1%; P=0.008); proportion of people with clinical expression of minimal symptoms (defined as having a MG-ADL score of 0 or 1) at any visit (25.4% vs 4.7%; P=0.004), and sustained MG-ADL improvement in the second treatment cycle (62.7% vs 36.4%; P=0.002). Batoclimab SC was generally well tolerated. The most frequently reported adverse event in the treatment group is peripheral edema (38.8% vs 4.6% for placebo), all of which were mild to moderate in severity. Plasma albumin levels decreased during treatment but returned spontaneously upon treatment discontinuation. "The approval of batoclimab SC is a proud moment for everyone at Harbour BioMed," Dr. Jingsong Wang, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Harbour BioMed, commented. "We believe that, with its unique mechanism of action, batoclimab SC has the potential to provide a new treatment option for patients with gMG. We are deeply grateful to the patients, investigators, and our partner for their trust and collaboration throughout this journey, and we look forward to making this therapy available to patients as quickly as possible, so that more people in need can benefit from it." "Batoclimab SC is the first FcRn-targeted therapy to complete its entire clinical development in China," Professor Chongbo Zhao, MD, Principal Investigator of the pivotal Phase 3 study and Professor of Neurology at Huashan Hospital of Fudan University, commented. "The trial results showed rapid onset of action, deep symptom improvement, and a favorable safety profile. This high-level evidence, based on data from Chinese patients, indicates that batoclimab SC provides a new treatment option for myasthenia gravis. This approval represents a monumental milestone in this field, and we believe it will bring a highly valuable new treatment option to physicians and patients in China." Pursuant to the license agreement entered into between Harbour BioMed and NBP Pharma on October, 2022, commercialization of batoclimab in the Greater China region (Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan) will be conducted by NBP Pharma, a subsidiary of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group. Harbour BioMed will receive tiered royalties based on annual net sales of batoclimab in Greater China. About Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG) Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a rare, chronic, autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. It is one of the most common forms of myasthenia gravis (MG), a disease mediated by antibodies such as anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) immunoglobulin G (IgG) and anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (Anti-MuSK) IgG. These antibodies target proteins at the postsynaptic membrane of the neuromuscular junction, causing impaired transmission and resulting in skeletal muscle weakness. gMG significantly affects patients' working status and quality of life, and some patients even develop myasthenic crisis, which can be life-threatening in severe cases. Currently, the main treatment options for gMG include cholinesterase inhibitors, glucocorticoids, and other immunosuppressive drugs. However, these therapies have a slow onset of action and are associated with significant side effects with long-term use. Plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) allow rapid clearance or neutralization of circulating pathogenic antibodies, but they are costly and unsustainable as hospital procedures. Overall, there remains a significant unmet need for these treatment options, including accessibility, safety, and economic cost. About Batoclimab and Batoclimab SC Batoclimab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). By blocking FcRn-mediated recycling of IgG antibodies, batoclimab accelerates the degradation of pathogenic IgG autoantibodies, offering a targeted therapeutic approach for autoimmune conditions including gMG. Batoclimab was originally developed by HanAll Biopharma Co., Ltd. ("HanAll") and licensed to Harbour BioMed in 2017 under a strategic collaboration and license agreement. Batoclimab SC is a subcutaneous biologic. The recommended dosing regimen is 680 mg once weekly; after 6 consecutive administrations, patients are observed for 4 weeks, making each treatment cycle a total of 9 weeks. Subcutaneous administration is convenient and easy to perform, reducing the time patients spend traveling to healthcare facilities and receiving intravenous infusions, thereby helping to alleviate the treatment burden and improve medication adherence. The marketing authorization holder (MAH) of batoclimab SC is Dragon Merit Holdings Limited, a subsidiary of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group. About Harbour Medical Harbour Medical is Harbour BioMed's core platform for clinical development and medical services, delivering integrated, end-to-end solutions for innovative therapies from early clinical validation through post-marketing studies. Serving both Harbour BioMed's internal pipeline and external partners, Harbour Medical brings together clinical development services, co-development, and strategic partnerships within a unified platform. With the Scientific Committee as our academic engine and an execution-driven team, Harbour Medical connects scientific innovation with clinical excellence, accelerating the journey of breakthrough therapies from the laboratory to patients. About Harbour BioMed Harbour BioMed (HKEX: 02142) is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to the discovery and development of novel antibody therapeutics in immunology, oncology and other areas. The Company is building a robust portfolio and differentiated pipeline through internal R&D capability, strategic global collaborations in co-discovery and co-development, and selective acquisitions. Our proprietary antibody technology platform, Harbour Mice®, generates fully human monoclonal antibodies in both the conventional two heavy and two light chain (H2L2) format and the heavy chain-only (HCAb) format. Building upon HCAb antibodies, the HCAb-based immune cell engagers (HBICE®) bispecific antibody technology enables tumor-killing effects that traditional combination therapies cannot achieve. The HCAb-based Antibody Plus technology (HCAb PLUSTM) provides comprehensive modality solutions for the development of innovative multi-specific medicines in different disease areas. Additionally, building upon the Harbour Mice® platform, Harbour BioMed launched its first fully human Generative AI HCAb Model powered by its Hu-mAtrIxTM AI platform, accelerating the development of innovative therapies. By integrating Harbour Mice®, HBICE®, HCAb PLUSTM, a single B-cell cloning platform and AI technologies, Harbour BioMed has built a highly efficient and distinctive antibody discovery engine for developing next-generation therapeutic antibodies. bd.title: Hanwha Power Receives ABS Approval in Principle for 1,700 TEU Battery-Powered Containership Design
bd.description: Fully electric propulsion design featuring approximately 151 MWh of energy storage strengthens capabilities in zero-carbon maritime transport Integrated solution combines electric propulsion, and containerized battery energy storage systems Expanded eco-friendly marine propulsion portfolio lays the groundwork for entry into the next-generation zero-carbon vessel market SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hanwha Power announced that it had received Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for its design of a 1,700 TEU battery-powered containership. Hanwha Power and ABS representatives at the AiP certificate presentation ceremony. The certificate presentation ceremony took place on October 22, local time, at the MHE (Maritime Hybrid, Electric & Hydrogen Fuel Cells) Conference & Exhibition 2026 in Bergen, Norway. Jong-kyu Hwang, Vice President, Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power, attended the ceremony alongside senior representatives from ABS. The event runs from October 21 to 23 at the Scandic Hotel Bergen City. The newly approved design concept features a fully electric container vessel powered by a large-scale 151 MWh Energy Storage System (ESS). Electrical energy stored in containerized battery units serves as the vessel's primary propulsion source, enabling operation without direct carbon emissions through the use of port charging infrastructure. The use of containerized batteries, which can be handled and stowed like standard cargo containers, enhances space efficiency, maximizes cargo capacity, and optimizes overall vessel performance. This approach also supports flexible battery replacement and scalable operation, offering a practical pathway for the decarbonization of short-sea and regional container transport. The AiP strengthens Hanwha Power's capabilities in fully electric vessel design using large-scale battery energy storage and expands its portfolio of marine propulsion solutions. The company plans to build on this achievement to pursue opportunities in the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market. Alongside the approval, Hanwha Power has also completed the basic design of a 1,000 TEU battery-powered container vessel. Building on its expertise in vessel design across multiple ship classes, the company aims to develop a comprehensive lineup of electric-propulsion vessels tailored to a wide range of operating conditions and customer needs. "This AiP from ABS marks an important step in extending Hanwha Power's marine technology capabilities to fully electric vessels powered by large-scale battery systems," said Jong-kyu Hwang, Vice President, Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power. "We will address the needs of the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market with integrated solutions that combine electric propulsion and containerized battery system technologies."

pk.title: Harbour BioMed Receives China NMPA Approval of Batoclimab Injection (Subcutaneous Injection) for the Treatment of Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
pk.description: The first NMPA-approved anti-FcRn therapy to complete its full clinical development for gMG patients in China CAMBRIDGE, Mass., ROTTERDAM, Netherlands and SHANGHAI, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbour BioMed (the "Company"; HKEX: 02142), a global biopharmaceutical company committed to the discovery and development of novel antibody therapeutics in immunology, oncology and other areas, today announced that the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China has approved the Biologics License Application (BLA) for batoclimab injection (subcutaneous injection) (batoclimab SC), 170 mg (1 mL)/vial, for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive. The approval is supported by positive results from a pivotal Phase 3 clinical study conducted at 27 centers in China. The main study population was patients with generalized myasthenia gravis who were positive for acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Ab) or muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies (MuSK-Ab). The primary endpoint of the study was the proportion of the population with sustained improvement in the Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living Scale (MG-ADL) score during the first cycle of treatment. Sustained improvement was defined as a reduction in MG-ADL score of ≥ 3 points from baseline that persisted for at least 4 weeks. 58.2% of patients treated with batoclimab SC achieved the primary endpoint, which was significantly higher compared with 31.3% in the placebo group (P=0.001). Treatment effect was observed as early as the second week of therapy. Additionally, batoclimab SC group demonstrated significant improvements in secondary endpoints compared with placebo group, including sustained Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) improvement (64.2% vs 40.6%; P=0.008), duration of 3-point or greater MG-ADL improvement (51.5% vs 36.1%; P=0.008); proportion of people with clinical expression of minimal symptoms (defined as having a MG-ADL score of 0 or 1) at any visit (25.4% vs 4.7%; P=0.004), and sustained MG-ADL improvement in the second treatment cycle (62.7% vs 36.4%; P=0.002). Batoclimab SC was generally well tolerated. The most frequently reported adverse event in the treatment group is peripheral edema (38.8% vs 4.6% for placebo), all of which were mild to moderate in severity. Plasma albumin levels decreased during treatment but returned spontaneously upon treatment discontinuation. "The approval of batoclimab SC is a proud moment for everyone at Harbour BioMed," Dr. Jingsong Wang, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Harbour BioMed, commented. "We believe that, with its unique mechanism of action, batoclimab SC has the potential to provide a new treatment option for patients with gMG. We are deeply grateful to the patients, investigators, and our partner for their trust and collaboration throughout this journey, and we look forward to making this therapy available to patients as quickly as possible, so that more people in need can benefit from it." "Batoclimab SC is the first FcRn-targeted therapy to complete its entire clinical development in China," Professor Chongbo Zhao, MD, Principal Investigator of the pivotal Phase 3 study and Professor of Neurology at Huashan Hospital of Fudan University, commented. "The trial results showed rapid onset of action, deep symptom improvement, and a favorable safety profile. This high-level evidence, based on data from Chinese patients, indicates that batoclimab SC provides a new treatment option for myasthenia gravis. This approval represents a monumental milestone in this field, and we believe it will bring a highly valuable new treatment option to physicians and patients in China." About Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG) Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a rare, chronic, autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. It is one of the most common forms of myasthenia gravis (MG), a disease mediated by antibodies such as anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) immunoglobulin G (IgG) and anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (Anti-MuSK) IgG. These antibodies target proteins at the postsynaptic membrane of the neuromuscular junction, causing impaired transmission and resulting in skeletal muscle weakness. gMG significantly affects patients' working status and quality of life, and some patients even develop myasthenic crisis, which can be life-threatening in severe cases. Currently, the main treatment options for gMG include cholinesterase inhibitors, glucocorticoids, and other immunosuppressive drugs. However, these therapies have a slow onset of action and are associated with significant side effects with long-term use. Plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) allow rapid clearance or neutralization of circulating pathogenic antibodies, but they are costly and unsustainable as hospital procedures. Overall, there remains a significant unmet need for these treatment options, including accessibility, safety, and economic cost. Our proprietary antibody technology platform, Harbour Mice®, generates fully human monoclonal antibodies in both the conventional two heavy and two light chain (H2L2) format and the heavy chain-only (HCAb) format. It is one of the most common forms of myasthenia gravis (MG), a disease mediated by antibodies such as anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) immunoglobulin G (IgG) and anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (Anti-MuSK) IgG. These antibodies target proteins at the postsynaptic membrane of the neuromuscular junction, causing impaired transmission and resulting in skeletal muscle weakness. gMG significantly affects patients' working status and quality of life, and some patients even develop myasthenic crisis, which can be life-threatening in severe cases. Currently, the main treatment options for gMG include cholinesterase inhibitors, glucocorticoids, and other immunosuppressive drugs. However, these therapies have a slow onset of action and are associated with significant side effects with long-term use. Plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) allow rapid clearance or neutralization of circulating pathogenic antibodies, but they are costly and unsustainable as hospital procedures. Overall, there remains a significant unmet need for these treatment options, including accessibility, safety, and economic cost. About Batoclimab and Batoclimab SC Batoclimab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). By blocking FcRn-mediated recycling of IgG antibodies, batoclimab accelerates the degradation of pathogenic IgG autoantibodies, offering a targeted therapeutic approach for autoimmune conditions including gMG. Batoclimab was originally developed by HanAll Biopharma Co., Ltd. ("HanAll") and licensed to Harbour BioMed in 2017 under a strategic collaboration and license agreement. Batoclimab SC is a subcutaneous biologic. The recommended dosing regimen is 680 mg once weekly; after 6 consecutive administrations, patients are observed for 4 weeks, making each treatment cycle a total of 9 weeks. Subcutaneous administration is convenient and easy to perform, reducing the time patients spend traveling to healthcare facilities and receiving intravenous infusions, thereby helping to alleviate the treatment burden and improve medication adherence. The marketing authorization holder (MAH) of batoclimab SC is Dragon Merit Holdings Limited, a subsidiary of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group. Serving both Harbour BioMed's internal pipeline and external partners, Harbour Medical brings together clinical development services, co-development, and strategic partnerships within a unified platform. With the Scientific Committee as our academic engine and an execution-driven team, Harbour Medical connects scientific innovation with clinical excellence, accelerating the journey of breakthrough therapies from the laboratory to patients. About Harbour BioMed Harbour BioMed (HKEX: 02142) is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to the discovery and development of novel antibody therapeutics in immunology, oncology and other areas. التي قدمتها دور النشر لتشجيع القراءة واقتناء الكتاب. ويقول سامر محمد، مدير مبيعات إحدى دور النشر العربية، لوكالة شفق نيوز: "هذه مشاركتنا السنوية الثابتة في معرض أربيل، وما يُميز اليوم الثاني هذا العام هو التنظيم العالي والوعي القرائي المتنامي لدى الجمهور الكوردي والعراقي بشكل عام". ويضيف محمد: "لاحظنا إقبالاً استثنائياً على الكتب الفكرية المترجمة والأعمال الأدبية الحديثة. أربيل تثبت دائماً أنها منصة حقيقية للتفاعل الثقافي الراقي". من جهته، يوضح الكاتب والباحث رێبوار أحمد، خلال جولة له في المعرض، لوكالة شفق نيوز، أن "معرض أربيل الدولي للكتاب ليس مجرد سوق لبيع الكتب، بل هو عرس ثقافي سنوي يلتقي فيه المثقفون من مختلف مدن العراق وإقليم كوردستان والعالم العربي". ويرى أحمد أن "وجود هذا الكم الهائل من دور النشر وتحت شعار معبر مثل (أنا كوردستاني) يعكس الوجه الحضاري المشرق لأربيل، ويؤكد أن الكتاب يظل الحصن الأقوى لمواجهة التحديات الفكرية". بدورها، تقول الشابة لارين عبد الله، طالبة جامعية وزائرة للمعرض، لوكالة شفق نيوز: "كنت أنتظر افتتاح المعرض بشغف كبير لتأجيل موعده السابق. حرصت على حضور فعاليات اليوم الثاني برفقة أصدقائي لاقتناء مجموعة من روايات الأدب العالمي والدراسات النفسية". وتؤكد عبد الله أن "أجواء المعرض مفعمة بالحياة، والخصومات المقدمة ساعدتنا في اقتناء عناوين جديدة كنا نتمنى الحصول عليها". ويستمر معرض أربيل الدولي للكتاب في استقبال زواره يومياً لمدة عشرة أيام من الساعة العاشرة صباحاً وحتى الثامنة مساءً، متضمناً في أيامه المقبلة جدولاً حافلاً بالندوات الثقافية، الأمسيات الشعرية، وجلسات توقيع الكتب لأبرز الوجوه الأدبية الفاعلة.

mg.title: AÉROPORT D’IVATO - La qualité de service irrite les usagers
mg.description: Demandes d’argent, fouilles contestées, contrôles mal compris : des passagers mettent en cause les pratiques de certains agents à l’aéroport international d’Ivato. Leurs témoignages soulèvent la question du traitement des plaintes et de l’identification des responsabilités. Plusieurs passagers expriment leur insatisfaction à l’égard des contrôles effectués à l’aéroport international d’Ivato. Ils font état de demandes insistantes d’argent ou de cadeaux de la part de certains agents, de procédures qui seraient volontairement ralenties et d’inspections qu’ils jugent arbitraires. Selon eux, ces pratiques viseraient à les inciter à payer pour accélérer leur passage. Des usagers dénoncent également les conditions de fouille et de manipulation de leurs bagages. « Lors de mon dernier voyage, des objets ont disparu de mes bagages et ma valise a été endommagée », a témoigné hier Stéphane, un passager. Les vérifications des documents de voyage suscitent aussi des interrogations. « Ma fille, qui partait étudier à l’étranger, a été bloquée à l’aéroport, soi-disant parce que son visa posait problème. Pourquoi la validité de son visa a-t-elle soudainement posé problème avant d’être acceptée dès le versement de quelques dollars ? », s’interroge un père de famille. Il dénonce une pression exercée « en dernière minute » pour contraindre les voyageurs à payer, sous la menace de manquer leur vol. Les contrôles approfondis portant sur les motifs de voyage, notamment ceux de jeunes femmes voyageant seules, sont une autre source d’incompréhension. La prévention de la traite des êtres humains et des recrutements illégaux figure parmi les objectifs invoqués pour justifier ces vérifications. Certains voyageurs en contestent toutefois les modalités et déplorent les retards qu’elles occasionnent. « Si on a un visa, c’est que notre motif de voyage est clair », poursuit ce père de famille. Sanctions Ces témoignages font écho à des plaintes déjà exprimées par le passé. Malgré les mesures annoncées il y a quelques années, des usagers continuent de signaler des pratiques similaires. « Oui, ces corruptions persistent à l’aéroport », affirme le sociologue Lanto Ratsida. « Ce n’est pas seulement un problème de comportement individuel, mais un problème structurel », estime-t-il. La multiplicité des intervenants pose la question de l’identification des responsabilités. Plusieurs entités exercent des missions distinctes à Ivato, parmi lesquelles l’Aviation civile de Madagascar (ACM), les douanes, la Police de l’air et des frontières (PAF), la Société de protection et de services de sécurité (SPSS) et l’Agence nationale de lutte contre les fraudes (ANAF). Pour les voyageurs, il n’est pas toujours aisé de savoir de quel service relève un contrôle ni à quelle entité appartient l’agent concerné. Lanto Ratsida avance plusieurs pistes pour renforcer la surveillance. « Il faut multiplier et surveiller nuit et jour les caméras de surveillance dans tous les endroits par où transitent les bagages (zone de tri, soute, etc.), et il ne doit y avoir aucune zone d’ombre », indique-t-il. Il préconise également des sanctions disciplinaires et des poursuites judiciaires lorsque des faits de vol ou de corruption sont établis. Selon lui, une amélioration des salaires et des avantages sociaux pourrait réduire la tentation de rechercher des « revenus complémentaires » illégaux. Il plaide enfin pour un contrôle indépendant, notamment par des audits externes, ainsi que pour une sensibilisation continue à l’éthique et à la déontologie. Reste la question du traitement des plaintes. Lorsqu’un passager dénonce un abus, il ne sait pas toujours à qui s’adresser. La présence de plusieurs intervenants peut compliquer ses démarches et l’identification des responsabilités. Des agents clairement identifiables, un canal de plainte accessible et une information sur les suites données aux signalements contribueraient à rendre les recours plus lisibles et à renforcer la confiance des usagers. Fanilo Mampianintsoa
